long_biography.plain_text:
At sixteen, Mark Dixon left school to deliver sandwiches on a butcher's bicycle. He experimented with peat, encyclopedia sales and logging before building a wholesale bread business, an early education in spotting routine customer frustrations. In Brussels, another such frustration appeared: travelling professionals were trying to conduct meetings around hotel and cafe tables.

Dixon responded in 1989 with a business centre offering equipped offices and services without long property commitments. Regus carried that model across borders, adding brands and adapting it for hybrid work. He spent nearly four decades leading the company before handing day-to-day management to Christian Schmitz in 2026. Dixon moved to the chair, where his remit centres on strategy and advice to the new chief executive.

uncertainties.detail: Mark Dixon is a common British name. The match rests on the conjunction of full legal name, November 1959 birth, British nationality, Monaco residence, Regus and IWG roles, and the existing exact Wikipedia profile. Unrelated businesspeople, athletes and public figures were excluded.

Companies House independently corroborates the full name and November 1959 but suppresses the day. Management Today's detailed founder chronology supplies 2 November and Hornchurch; those fields are proposed at 92 rather than treating the existing Wikipedia page alone as authoritative.

The source biography and some older company pages call Dixon chief executive. IWG's board page and 16 June 2026 RNS establish that he became executive chair and Christian Schmitz became chief executive, so the proposed title and biography use the current role.

IWG's annual report documents that Dixon owns all of Estorn Limited and that Estorn held 25.8% of IWG as of 13 March 2026. This is a substantial and largest disclosed stake, not ownership of the whole company; executive-chair status and influence do not convert minority shareholding into complete control.

IWG's market capitalisation, enterprise value, revenue, workspace network, leases, cash, debt and operating assets belong to the listed company. Dixon's personally evidenced economic interest is his Estorn-held shareholding and associated compensation or awards, not the full value of those corporate assets.

Forbes notes a separate English winery, but no source reviewed demonstrates that it rivals the IWG shareholding as the principal current wealth base. It therefore does not alter the Real Estate primary-industry classification.

The existing Wikipedia profile matches the resolved founder. No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the acceptance threshold; only the dedicated Forbes profile and current IWG board page are proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel research were excluded. None contributes to the identity, classification or biography claims.
